_doc: Cross-layer call_digest vectors (microsoft/autogen#7405 GuardrailProvider RFC, issuecomment-5933530423). action_ref correlates one attempt's records across layers (preimage: {agent_id, action_type, scope, timestamp}, no arguments); call_digest binds what the call actually was (preimage: {tool_name, arguments}), recomputable by a layer that never sees agent_id or scope. The two are deliberately different primitives, not duplicates -- this fixture demonstrates all three joins a verifier needs: same call seen by two layers that disagree (A), the same call rewritten before dispatch (B), and a call that never reached an inner layer at all (C).

spec_refs.fixture_reused: giskard09/argentum-core examples/conformance/guardrail-provider-v1.fixture.json, same commit, referenced with author confirmation (microsoft/autogen#7405#issuecomment-5934214515: "Confirmed -- go ahead and reference it")
spec_refs.not_reached_marker: babyblueviper1/invinoveritas integrations/autogen/governed_workbench.py (commit bd06127), the on_not_reached marker proposed and shipped on this same thread (#7405#issuecomment-5299618444 / 5299678449)

canonicalization.note: Matches giskard09's reproduce_in_python dispatch for action_ref/authorization_ref/args digests, so all values in this fixture recompute under one rule.

shared_context.description: action_ref and authorization_ref are reused verbatim from the pinned guardrail-provider-v1 fixture (recomputed and confirmed matching in issuecomment-5933530423). Vectors A and B both concern this one attempt.

vector_a_provider_approve_gate_deny.label: Two independently-emitted layer records about the SAME call disagree on verdict
vector_a_provider_approve_gate_deny.description: A provider layer approves the call (dispatched args == effective_args, no revision). A separate gate layer evaluates the identical call and denies it for a policy reason the provider layer has no visibility into. Both layers compute call_digest from only {tool_name, arguments} -- neither needs the other's record to do it. A verifier recomputes both call_digests, confirms they're equal (same call), and that the deny wins (no receipt exists for this action_ref + call_digest pair).
vector_a_provider_approve_gate_deny.invariant: provider_record.call_digest == gate_record.call_digest (confirmed same call) AND gate verdict == deny => no receipt exists for (action_ref, call_digest)

vector_b_rewrite.label: A call rewritten before dispatch produces two different call_digests
vector_b_rewrite.description: The provider proposes original_args; a guardrail revises them before the call executes. proposed_call_digest and effective_call_digest differ -- this is the two-number join call_digest already requires for a rewrite (distinct from the single-call case in Vector A). Deliberately NOT equal to giskard09's original_args_digest/effective_args_digest: those bind args alone, call_digest additionally folds in tool_name, so a layer with no scope/agent_id visibility can still recompute it. The two primitives are complementary, not duplicates.
invariants: proposed_call_digest != effective_call_digest (rewrite is visible at the call_digest layer)
original_args_digest != effective_args_digest (rewrite is visible at giskard09's args-digest layer too, independently)
effective_call_digest != effective_args_digest (same args, different preimage shape -- tool_name changes the binding)

vector_c_not_reached.label: A call that never reached the inner layer carries no call_digest at all
vector_c_not_reached.description: A second, independent attempt. An outer gate denies before ever delegating to an inner provider -- the inner provider never receives the call and therefore never computes a call_digest for it. This is the not_reached marker shape proposed and shipped on this thread (babyblueviper1/invinoveritas commit bd06127, integrations/autogen/governed_workbench.py): {provider_id, reason}, no call fields, because none exist yet to hash. A verifier must read 'no call_digest field' here as 'never attempted', distinct from a record that carries a call_digest field with a null/empty value (which would mean a bug).
vector_c_not_reached.invariant: inner_not_reached_marker has no call_digest key at all (provider never saw the call) while outer_terminal_record carries its own action_ref/verdict for the attempt the outer gate DID evaluate

vector_d_number_canonicalization._doc: The call_digest preimage must be RFC 8785 JCS, not a language's default JSON serializer: Python json.dumps and ECMAScript JSON.stringify disagree on number text (1e-07 vs 1e-7, 1e+16 vs 10000000000000000, -0.0 vs 0, floats above 2^53). A layer that hashes with the wrong serializer computes a different call_digest for the same call and the cross-layer join silently fails. canonical_args_rfc8785 was produced by Node JSON.stringify (v22) and is reproduced byte for byte by examples/cross-layer-call-digest-vectors/rfc8785.py (stdlib only). The preimage member name for the arguments object is not pinned by the RFC text yet, so both digests are given: call_digest_arguments = sha256(JCS({tool_name, arguments})) as used in vectors A-C, call_digest_tool_input = sha256(JCS({tool_name, tool_input})). tool_name is 'calc.run' throughout.
